football_evidence.assessment: EdgeDesk’s number is 5.0 points closer to Rice than the line, and EdgeDesk cannot account for most of that: its own breakdown accounts for about 1.5 of the 5.0 points. The measured football evidence leans toward Tulsa, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.

When Tulsa has the ball (the red zone): Tulsa’s offense succeeds on 34.3% of its red-zone plays, and Rice’s defense allows success on 35.3% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.8%).
When Tulsa has the ball (third down): Tulsa’s offense converts 29.3% of its third downs, and Rice’s defense allows opponents to convert 38.5% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Tulsa has the ball (big plays through the air): Tulsa’s offense turns 8.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Rice’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).
contradicting: When Rice has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Rice’s offense has allowed a sack on 11.3% of its dropbacks, and Tulsa’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Rice has the ball (big plays through the air): Rice’s offense turns 6.6% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Tulsa’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.0% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).

When Tulsa has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Tulsa’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.9% of its dropbacks, and Rice’s defense sacks the quarterback on 4.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Tulsa has the ball (big plays on the ground): Tulsa’s offense turns 5.4% of its runs into explosive gains, and Rice’s defense gives up explosive gains on 11.1% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
quarterbacks: Jacurri Brown has completed 38 of 77 passes (49.4%) for 431 yards, 5.6 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in six games for Rice, and has been sacked on 9 of 86 dropbacks.
Baylor Hayes has completed 80 of 132 passes (60.6%) for 832 yards, 6.3 yards per attempt, 5 touchdowns and 1 interception in four games for Tulsa, and has been sacked on 5 of 137 dropbacks.
Dexter Williams II has completed 34 of 60 passes (56.7%) for 340 yards, 5.7 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and no interceptions in three games for Tulsa, and has been sacked on 3 of 63 dropbacks.
